thread:
Renee: Vendor "DataBridge EU" says they paid local VAT and asks Redwood to gross-up the net amount because refund of the VAT via local reclaim will take 6-9 months. Invoice DB-EU-304 (EUR 20,000 + EUR 4,000 VAT). They request gross-up to EUR 24,000 so they get full EUR 20k now. PDF: https://invoices.example.com/DB-EU-304.pdf

Gabe: We don't have a standing gross-up policy for vendor VAT timing. Contractually vendor bears VAT unless invoice issued net to a VAT-registered buyer. Did vendor charge VAT incorrectly (i.e., they should have zero-rated the sale to our EU VAT ID)?

Marta: AP note: PO billed to Redwood EU with VAT ID IE-334455. Vendor included local FR VAT (FR123456789). Looks like they billed as domestic sale. We asked for reissue net but vendor says their system can't reissue quickly and asks for gross-up instead.

AP: Holding payment until resolved. If we gross-up, procurement/legal must approve and we need an amendment capturing one-off gross-up and attach proof vendor will claim refund.

Gabe: TaxOps: options: (1) Insist on reissue net and hold until they can produce it or credit memo; (2) Accept credit memo path where vendor issues credit for VAT and we pay net; (3) Exceptional gross-up but require vendor to assign refund claim to Redwood or provide indemnity. My preference: no gross-ups unless legal signs off.

Marta: Practical: vendor says client cashflow hit. If we ask for credit memo + new net invoice that's best for audit. Vendor replies they can issue a credit memo but needs a purchase order change. AP: can you accept credit memo + new invoice and expedite internal PO change?

AP: We can process credit memo if vendor provides it and matches original invoice references. Will need Coupa upload and AP ticket. No gross-up without documented approval.

invoice-bot: Event: invoice_hold placed (invoice=DB-EU-304, reason=vat_reclaim_delay_request)

Gabe: Closing: Renee please tell vendor we prefer credit memo + reissue net. If vendor refuses and insists on gross-up, escalate to Legal/Finance leadership with vendor repayment/assignment terms. Thanks.
